legend: You are given an undirected tree with n$$$n$$$ vertices, labeled from 0$$$0$$$ to n−1$$$n-1$$$. The tree has n−1$$$n-1$$$ edges and is connected and acyclic.
Your task is to select exactly k$$$k$$$ vertices (2≤k≤n$$$2 \leq k \leq n$$$) such that the minimum MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ value over all paths between two chosen vertices is maximized.

For any two vertices u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$, define Puv$$$P_{uv}$$$ as the set of vertex labels that appear on the unique simple path between them. The function MEX(Puv)$$$\operatorname{MEX}(P_{uv})$$$ is defined as the smallest non-negative integer that does not appear in Puv$$$P_{uv}$$$.
Formally, for a chosen set of vertices S$$$S$$$ with |S|=k$$$|S| = k$$$, we define: f(S)=minu,v∈S,u≠vMEX(Puv).$$ f(S) = \min_{u, v \in S, u \neq v} \operatorname{MEX}(P_{uv}). $$
Your goal is to maximize f(S)$$$f(S)$$$ over all valid choices of S$$$S$$$.
For each integer k$$$k$$$ from 2$$$2$$$ to n$$$n$$$, compute the maximum possible value of f(S)$$$f(S)$$$.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (3≤n≤105)$$$(3 \leq n \leq 10^5)$$$ — the number of nodes in the tree.
The next n−1$$$n-1$$$ lines each contain two integers u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ (0≤u,v<n)$$$(0 \leq u, v  \lt  n)$$$, representing an undirected edge between nodes u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, print n−1$$$n-1$$$ integers. The i$$$i$$$-th integer should represent the maximum possible value of the minimum MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ when choosing k=i+1$$$k = i+1$$$ nodes.
note: The given tree has n=5$$$n = 5$$$ nodes with the following structure:
Node 0$$$0$$$ is connected to nodes 1$$$1$$$ and 2$$$2$$$.
Node 1$$$1$$$ is connected to nodes 3$$$3$$$ and 4$$$4$$$.
For k=2$$$k = 2$$$, selecting nodes {2,3}$$$\{2, 3\}$$$ maximizes f(S)$$$f(S)$$$, yielding MEX(P2,3)=4$$$\operatorname{MEX}(\mathcal{P}_{2,3}) = 4$$$.
For k=3$$$k = 3$$$, selecting nodes {0,1,2}$$$\{0, 1, 2\}$$$ yields a maximum f(S)=1$$$f(S) = 1$$$.
For k=4$$$k = 4$$$ and k=5$$$k = 5$$$, the maximum value of f(S)$$$f(S)$$$ is 0$$$0$$$.
